intro: Self-imposed habits that keep Henry feeling like Henry. Pick the ones you like — none are required.
source: Collected from long-standing r/kingdomcome role-play advice and the KCD1 wiki. Reddit blocked live access while this guide was built, so treat these as community conventions, not hard rules.

groups.title: Before you start
rules: Hardcore Mode (new game only): no compass, no player marker on the map, and negative perks you pick. It's the biggest immersion boost, and it's harder.
Learn to read the map by landmarks — roads, rivers, church towers — instead of following the quest marker.

groups.title: Living as Henry
rules: Sleep at night in a bed you own or have rented. Eat proper meals instead of waiting for the hunger warning.
Wash and mend your clothes before meeting nobles. Charisma changes how people react, and a bloody Henry at Radzig's table makes no sense.
Save sparingly: sleep in your own bed or drink Saviour Schnapps only before genuinely risky moments.
Walk inside towns, carry a torch at night, and only draw a weapon when there's a reason to.

groups.title: Gear that fits the story
rules: Before Awakening, Henry is a penniless refugee: plain clothes and a cheap weapon, no shining plate.
Upgrade to real armour once Radzig takes you into service — bought, earned or taken from bandits, not stripped from honest townsfolk.
Keep Cuman gear for Masquerade and Nest of Vipers. Wearing it around villages otherwise makes no sense.
Dress for the occasion: noble clothes for Capon's errands, a habit in the monastery, hunting gear in the woods.

groups.title: Travel
rules: Fast travel is fair game, since time passes and ambushes happen. Still, ride the road for the big moments: the flight to Talmberg, Pribyslavitz, Vranik.
Don't climb cliffs on horseback or jump walls to skip a gate.

groups.title: Crime & conscience
rules: Steal only when Henry has a reason: the Peshek arc, charity for the refugees, or a quest. Never rob friends who helped him.
Let surrendering enemies flee. Don't strip unconscious townsfolk.
Henry is a blacksmith's son, not a killer. Keep early fights to fists and knock-outs where you can.

groups.title: Pacing
rules: Don't rush the main story after Awakening. The route deliberately spreads side jobs between main beats.
Finish timed quests in one go. They're written as urgent, so play them that way.
Respect NPC routines: shops in the day, nobles in the morning, rest at night.
Don't skip cutscenes or dialogue — that's where Henry's growth happens.

2: Henry arrives with nothing: no armour, no sword of his own, no gold. Keep it that way until he earns it.
17: From the moment the scribe's lessons end, Henry can read — that's when to start using skill books.
45: Henry is finally in Radzig's service. Now is the time to equip proper armour and a real sword.
50: Rest, eat and bathe the night before. Henry rides into his first real battle at dawn.
104: Live by the bell: mass, meals, work, sleep. Skipping the timetable gets you punished, and it breaks the illusion.
112: Before leaving, take a farewell tour: Theresa, Matthew and Fritz, Peshek, and your parents' graves in Skalitz.
